recent_articles.title: Unlike Centre, Sindh announces four Eid holidays - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah** issued a notification extending the Eidul Azha holiday in the province to four days, from May 26th to May 29th, 2026. The holiday applies to all government offices, autonomous bodies, semi-autonomous bodies, corporations, and local councils, except for essential services and departments/offices preparing the budget for the fiscal year 2026-27.

recent_articles.title: Meet demands or face budget boycott, Achakzai tells govt - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mehmood Khan Achakzai**, leader of the opposition in the National Assembly, warned **Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif** that the upcoming budget session would be a complete boycott if the government does not meet their demands for Imran Khan's medical treatment and unrestricted visitation rights.  He also criticized the lackluster attendance from the treasury benches as evidence of the government's disregard for parliament. Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, chairman of the **PTI**, accused the government of suppressing dissent and police excesses against those attempting to visit Imran Khan in prison.

recent_articles.title: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto inaugurates 39km-long Shahrah-i-Bhutto linking Qayyumabad to M9 Motorway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari** inaugurated the 39-kilometer Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway, linking Karachi's Qayyumabad to the M-9 Motorway.  He also laid the foundation stone for a new expressway project connecting Karachi Port to Qayyumabad. **Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah** highlighted the expressway's six interchanges, lanes, and elevated section, emphasizing its potential to reduce travel time by an hour. **Bilawal Bhutto Zardari** emphasized the PPP's commitment to public-private partnerships in developing Karachi and Pakistan, citing projects worth billions of rupees underway. He also announced plans for a Sindh International Financial Centre and a defense production zone in Karachi.

recent_articles.title: Picked wrong Melody? Parle Industries shares hit 5% upper circuit for 3rd day - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: During a visit to Italy, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** gifted **Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni** a bag of candies called "Melody." The viral video of the exchange sparked interest in Indian brands and led to marketing campaigns by companies like **Air India**.  The candy's maker, **Parle Products**, confirmed it is exported to 100 countries. While Parle Industries shares saw a significant jump following the incident, the company has no immediate plans for an initial public offering.

recent_articles.title: Babar, Naseem recalled as PCB announces 16-member squad for Australia ODIs - Sport - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)** announced a 16-member squad for the upcoming three-match ODI series against **Australia**, scheduled from May 30 to June 4. The squad includes players like **Shaheen Shah Afridi** (captain) and **Babar Azam**, who were not part of the recent Bangladesh series.  The team will assemble in Islamabad on Friday and begin training on Saturday, with the Australian team arriving in Islamabad on Saturday as well.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh leaders to meet Home Ministry officials on May 22, Sonam Wangchuk part of delegation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Ladakh, including climate activist **Sonam Wangchuk**, is meeting with **Union Home Ministry** officials on Friday to discuss demands for constitutional safeguards such as Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. This meeting follows a previous inconclusive high-powered committee meeting in February and comes after the violence in Leh city in September 2025, which stalled talks.  The delegation will reiterate their demands for Statehood, while officials have offered safeguards under Article 371 of the Constitution.

recent_articles.title: Bihar midday meal incident: HC asks whether NGO can continue providing meals - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Patna High Court** has expressed concern over delays in the investigation of a midday meal incident where over 150 students fell ill in Saharsa district. The court questioned whether the NGO supplying meals to over 1,800 students should continue operations during the probe and raised concerns about discrepancies in food sample collection and testing.  The court directed officials to file affidavits explaining the processes involved. The matter will be heard again on June 2nd.

recent_articles.title: Seems PTI will now have to 'resort to agitation', says MNA after party leaders yet again denied meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ahad Ali Shah**, a member of the **Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)**, stated that his party would resort to agitation after being denied another meeting with former prime minister **Imran Khan**.  The Islamabad High Court has granted **Khan** twice-weekly meetings at Adiala jail, but restrictions have prevented him from meeting visitors for several weeks. The PTI submitted a list of six leaders, including Shah, for a meeting on Thursday but was denied access.  A caravan led by **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi** to meet **Khan** was stopped in Islamabad and resulted in a sit-in at Chungi No. 26.

recent_articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress** party, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and supporting industrialists. He also warned of an impending economic crisis, stating that it would disproportionately affect ordinary citizens while benefiting those in power.  Gandhi unveiled a statue of Veera Pasi in Rae Bareli, highlighting his party's renewed focus on the community. He further criticized the BJP government over land acquisition policies and unemployment rates, vowing to fight for the rights of the people.

recent_articles.title: Fatima Sana to lead women’s side as PCB announces squad for T20 World Cup, Ireland tri-series - Sport - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)** announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, including captain **Fatima Sana**, who will lead the team for the second consecutive tournament. The squad will participate in a tri-series featuring Ireland and the West Indies from May 28 to June 4 before traveling to England and Wales for the main event.  The Pakistan women's team will play warm-up matches against Sri Lanka and Scotland before beginning their campaign against India on June 14.

recent_articles.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.sentiment_target: State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Lahore High Court** upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments from **State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan**. The court rejected the corporation's arguments that Section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 was no longer enforceable due to Islamic injunctions. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed all four appeals filed by the corporation and ordered the payment of statutory interest at a rate five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of death of each insured person until realization of the amount.  The court also rejected objections regarding limitation and maintainability, noting that the claimants had pursued remedies in good faith despite confusion regarding the proper legal forum for insurance disputes.

recent_articles.title: Lawmakers decry slow internet in National Assembly, across country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several members of the **National Assembly** raised concerns about slow internet connectivity affecting the paperless working environment in parliament.  **Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah** directed authorities to address the issue, while **Federal Information Technology and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja** assured them that the spectrum auction would improve internet facilities. **Khawaja** also addressed concerns over digital harassment, online fraud, and data theft, emphasizing public awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant institutions.

recent_articles.title: Semi-high-speed train project to turn Gujarat into manufacturing and logistics hub: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, announced that the Cabinet approved a ₹20,667 crore Ahmedabad (Sarkhej)-Dholera semi-high-speed double rail line project. The project will connect Ahmedabad to Dholera Special Investment Region and Greenfield Industrial Smart City, creating employment opportunities and positioning Gujarat as a global manufacturing hub.  **Shah** also lauded the Cabinet's decision to upgrade and modernize the Nagpur International Airport and a ₹37,500 crore scheme for surface coal and lignite gasification projects, which will contribute to India's economic growth and job creation.

recent_articles.title: Efforts on to release Kuki, Naga people held hostage in Manipur, say Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the killings of four church leaders in separate ambushes, **Govindas Konthoujam**, **Losii Dikho** and other officials confirmed that at least 38 people from the Kuki and Naga communities are being held hostage by various groups.  The attacks occurred in the Kuki-dominated Kangpokpi district and the Naga-majority Noney district. The Deputy Chief Minister stated that talks were ongoing with both Kuki and Naga groups, but no resolution was reached. **Angomcha Bimol Akoijam**, a Manipur Congress MP, criticized the government's handling of the situation.  The United Naga Council (UNC) issued an ultimatum to the state government demanding the release of 20 hostages held by Kuki groups.

recent_articles.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa's 'zombie drug' and opioid crisis despite crackdown - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Indian pharmaceutical companies are exporting high-strength tapentadol tablets to west Africa despite a crackdown on illegal drug trade. The pills, which are often sold as tramadol and are much stronger than approved doses, are fueling a deadly opioid epidemic in the region.  The pills are being added to "zombie drugs" like kush, leading to increased addiction and health problems, including deaths from overdoses.  While India claims it has banned exports of tapentadol mixed with other drugs, shipments continue despite warnings from government officials in Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Ghana. The Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association defends the trade, stating that manufacturers are not responsible for what happens after their products leave their facilities. Experts warn that the lack of regulation and enforcement in Africa allows unscrupulous companies to exploit the market, leading to widespread misuse of the drug.

recent_articles.title: Karachi's Shahrah-i-Bhutto to be fully open to public by end of May: Sharjeel Memon - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sindh** Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon announced the full opening of the Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway in Karachi by the end of May, a 39-kilometer high-speed corridor that will connect to the M-9 highway.  Memon stated the project is expected to save commuters at least an hour traveling into the city and improve traffic flow. **Sindh** Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had previously directed for full operationalization by April 2026. Additionally, Memon announced a new road connecting Karachi Port with the Taj Haider Bridge, which will be completed around the same time as the expressway's opening.  Memon highlighted that these projects are part of a larger effort to improve connectivity and convenience in **Karachi**.

recent_articles.title: Trump taps David Venturella, former private prison executive, to lead ICE | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump's** administration has appointed **David Venturella**, a former executive at the private prison company GEO Group, as acting director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Venturella will replace Todd Lyons, who is leaving the agency on May 31st.  Venturella previously served at ICE under both Democratic and Republican administrations and has been involved in the Trump administration's mass deportation campaign, which has benefited private contractors like GEO Group. Rights groups have criticized the hiring of Venturella as a "revolving-door phenomenon" due to his past experience with ICE and GEO Group.

recent_articles.title: IHC rules high courts can assume jurisdiction in cases of promotion assessments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Islamabad High Court** ruled that high courts can review decisions made by the **Central Selection Board (CSB)** regarding promotions for top bureaucrats. The court overturned the CSB's supersession and deferment of several officers, including those from the Police Service of Pakistan, Pakistan Administrative Service, Inland Revenue Service, Pakistan Customs Service, and health sector.  The court found that the CSB’s decision-making process lacked fairness and transparency, citing procedural impropriety in communication of reasons for decisions. The judgment emphasized constitutional guarantees of fairness and due process, directing the Federation to reconsider promotions based on merit and fitness.

recent_articles.title: Khawaja Asif says KP now on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Defence Minister Khawaja Asif** acknowledged that the **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** government is now cooperating with the federal government in combating terrorism. He stated that despite past disagreements, the two governments are united in their efforts to address the issue and emphasized Pakistan's attempts to engage with the Afghan Taliban for a peaceful resolution.  Asif also addressed concerns about terrorist activities originating from Afghanistan, highlighting the need for cooperation from all provinces and the ongoing challenges faced by Pakistani forces. Following a heated exchange between **Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl** leader Noor Alam Khan and Asif during a parliamentary session, Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah adjourned the session due to unruly behavior from PTI members.

recent_articles.title: PM austerity appeal: State leaders take steps to limit their fuel use - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and several other state chief ministers have implemented measures to reduce fuel consumption in response to the West Asia crisis.  These include reducing convoy sizes, promoting electric vehicles, and encouraging public transport use. **Yogi Adityanath**, **Rekha Gupta**, **Mohan Yadav**, and others have also taken steps to promote sustainability within their respective states.  **Devendra Fadnavis**, **Harsh Sanghavi**, and **Acharya Devvrat** have implemented similar measures in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Bihar respectively.

recent_articles.title: Sensing an edge, Iran 'ready to gamble' it can outlast Trump - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Iran**’s leadership is betting it can outlast **Donald Trump** in its peace negotiations, despite the US president's warnings of a looming truce collapse.  Analysts believe Iran understands that blocking the Strait of Hormuz gives it leverage and is willing to endure economic hardship for a chance at favorable terms. However, they also acknowledge the risk of renewed conflict as Iran faces internal dissent and struggles with damage from US-Israeli attacks. **Trump**’s administration is under pressure to find an exit strategy, but analysts believe that neither side wants full-scale hostilities.

recent_articles.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh win first home Test against Pakistan | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh** defeated **Pakistan** by 104 runs in the first Test match at Dhaka, securing their maiden home Test victory.  Pace bowler **Nahid Rana** claimed five wickets as Bangladesh bowled out **Pakistan** for 163 on the final day after a rain-interrupted contest. **Najmul Hossain Shanto**, captain of **Bangladesh**, achieved a significant milestone by equaling **Mushfiqur Rahim's** record of seven Test wins as captain, while **Rana** delivered career-best figures of 5-40 to secure the victory. The two teams will now play the second Test in Sylhet on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Assam swearing-in LIVE: Himanta Biswa Sarma takes oath as Assam CM; Four MLAs sworn in as Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term on Tuesday, May 2, 2026. **Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya** administered the oath of office at a ceremony held at the Veterinary Ground in Guwahati.  Joining **Sarma** were four other MLAs who took oaths as Ministers: **Rameswar Teli**, **Ajanta Neog**, **Atul Bora**, and **Charan Boro**. The event was attended by prominent figures including **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, Nitin Gadkari, Sarbananda Sonowal, Pabitra Margherita**, and **BJP president Nitin Nabin**. This marks the formation of a third successive NDA government in the state.

recent_articles.title: $200 million divorce battle: Iranian heiress accused of shielding family assets to block husband’s claims in California - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Setareh “Star” Bral**, daughter of a late Iranian real estate tycoon, is accused by her estranged husband, **Ryan Aronin**, of hiding assets in a $200 million divorce battle.  Court documents allege that Bral transferred control of her company, Star Pacific Properties, to her brother in October 2024 and attempted to distance herself from the SYB Family Trust, which is estimated to be worth $200 million. Aronin claims she has continued to benefit from trust-related rental income despite separating from him in March 2022. The dispute centers around Bral's alleged attempts to limit her financial exposure and control over assets.

recent_articles.title: Most drowning cases occur in summer: Fire dept. - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Fire and Rescue Services** department reported a surge in drowning cases involving students during summer vacation.  Three dental students from **Baselios Dental College** drowned in the Palavan river near Kothamangalam, while another student drowned in a quarry in Thrikkariyoor panchayat. The incidents highlight the dangers of strong undercurrents and deep pits in the picturesque but treacherous river. To address this issue, **Kothamangalam fire station** organized a 10-day swimming camp for students.

recent_articles.title: Skipper Shanto extends Bangladesh lead by 179 runs in first Test against Pakistan - Sport - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh** extended their lead over **Pakistan** to 179 runs on the fourth day of the first Test match in Dhaka.  **Najmul Hossain Shanto** hit an unbeaten half-century, while **Mominul Haque** reached a fifty before being dismissed. The hosts were 152-3 at stumps with **Shanto** and **Mushfiqur Rahim** remaining unbeaten. Pakistan's **Mohammad Rizwan** failed to hold on to a catch, but the afternoon session was washed out by heavy rain.  The final day promises to be an exciting one for fans as both teams battle for victory.

recent_articles.title: Justice Aurangzeb calls for encouraging alternative dispute resolution, says SC to establish mediation centre - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb**, of the **Supreme Court of Pakistan**, urged the judiciary to encourage alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and highlighted the Supreme Court's efforts in establishing a mediation center.  He emphasized the need for more judges to be trained as mediators, with financial assistance from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), to make mediation accessible to all parties. **Justice Aurangzeb** also noted that while there is no shortage of mediators in Pakistan, they must be compensated fairly for their expertise and services. He stressed the importance of a well-equipped and comfortable mediation center to encourage its use.  The Supreme Court's initiative follows previous calls from **Syed Mansoor Ali Shah**, former senior puisne judge, for adopting ADR mechanisms to address the growing backlog of cases.

recent_articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant** praised **Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's** new books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous anecdotes from the courtroom.  Kant suggested that Mehta likely wrote the books during downtime in court or while waiting for slow-moving files to be read.  **Home Minister Amit Shah** also attended the book launch.

recent_articles.title: Solicitor General launches two tomes on humour in court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant** praised **Solicitor General Tushar Mehta's** books, "The Bench, The Bar and The Bizarre" and "The Lawful and The Awful," which feature humorous courtroom anecdotes.  **Kant** suggested that the books were filled with comical tales from the Indian legal system, noting that there was ample material in Delhi alone to fill a library. **Shah**, the Home Minister, also attended the launch event.

recent_articles.title: CM selection a democratic process: Chennithala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramesh Chennithala**, a senior Congress leader, criticized the BJP for its alleged delay in selecting a Chief Minister after the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections. He defended the **Congress**'s democratic process and emphasized that decisions are made through discussions within the party.  Chennithala stated that five days is not an unreasonable time frame for such a decision, especially considering the complexity of the selection process. The Congress leadership has been meeting with various leaders to arrive at a consensus on the next Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: Crumbling of Awadh’s heritage amidst monument encroachments - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) highlights the concerning state of protected monuments in Uttar Pradesh. The report found that 31 centrally protected monuments are untraceable, with only 31 monuments having proper ownership documentation and 96 being encroached upon. Heritage activists express worry over the disappearance of these historical sites and the potential loss of Awadhi culture, which is intertwined with the architecture and traditions of these structures.  The report also found that the ASI has not been adequately enforcing existing laws and regulations, leading to inadequate planning and documentation for conservation efforts. Experts advocate for stronger legislation, including a state heritage law, to address this issue and protect these valuable cultural assets.

recent_articles.title: No one is buying Trump's Gold? Immigration attorneys say the $1 million visa scheme is 'unethical' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several immigration lawyers are advising wealthy foreigners to avoid **Donald Trump**'s "Gold Card" visa program due to legal and financial concerns.  The program, which costs between $1 million and $2 million, has not been approved by Congress and faces uncertainty about its future. Attorneys warn that the program is risky and may lead to financial loss for applicants, citing ongoing litigation, tax complications, and potential cancellation by a future administration. Despite these concerns, some individuals are still pursuing applications, but interest in the program remains far below initial projections.

recent_articles.title: Indian-American Tina Shah stirs row after saying she is the ‘only Democrat who is pro-Israel’ in viral video - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tina Shah**, an Indian-American congressional candidate in New Jersey, sparked controversy after a leaked audio clip revealed her describing herself as the only Democrat in her race fully backing Israel. The recording reignited debate within the progressive party over foreign policy issues like the Gaza war and tensions with Iran.  Progressive lawmakers such as **Bernie Sanders** and **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** have criticized US military aid to Israel, while other Democrats, including **John Fetterman** and **Chuck Schumer**, support continued military aid and a strong stance in favor of Israel.

recent_articles.title: JCP likely to finalise panel to interview candidates - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP)** is expected to decide on a committee structure for interviewing candidates for high court appointments during its upcoming meeting. The move has raised concerns from lawyers who argue that interviews should not be conducted by committees outside the constitutional framework.  The JCP's Rule-Making Committee discussed various proposals, including a seven-member committee conducting interviews prior to the full commission meeting and a five-member committee comprising judges, parliamentarians, the attorney general, and a representative of the Pakistan Bar Council. The proposals will be presented to the full commission next week, potentially leading to the finalization of new rules governing judicial appointments.

recent_articles.title: NDA leaders stake claim to form Assam government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**-led **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was unanimously elected as the leader of the Assam Legislature Party.  Following this, the NDA staked a claim to form the government in Assam with the support of 102 MLAs. The swearing-in ceremony for the new council of ministers is scheduled for May 12th. **J.P. Nadda**, Union Minister and central observer for the BJP Legislature Party meeting, announced that eight BJP legislators proposed Sarma's name as their leader.  The newly elected members of the BJP and its regional allies — **Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)** and **Bodoland People’s Front (BPF)** — chose their leaders in the morning.

recent_articles.title: Ministers, ambassadors, artists to join The Hindu’s Huddle in June - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Hindu Group** is hosting its annual **The Hindu Huddle**, a conference focused on global issues, in Bengaluru from June 5th to 6th. This year's theme, "A World in Transition," will feature discussions on topics such as regional parties in Indian democracy, diplomacy and conflict resolution, women's representation in Parliament, the role of AI, mental health, and the future of work.  The event will include prominent speakers from India and around the world, including Union Ministers Hardeep Puri and Nitin Gadkari, former President Mohamed Nasheed, and Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong.

recent_articles.title: Abbas takes five wickets to put Pakistan ahead in Bangladesh Test - Sport - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohammad Abbas** claimed five wickets for **Pakistan**, restricting **Bangladesh** to 413 runs on the second day of the first Test in Dhaka.  **Azan Awais** and **Abdullah Fazal** combined for an unbeaten partnership of 179, giving **Pakistan** a strong start at 179-1. **Bangladesh** captain **Najmul Hossain Shanto** scored 101 on the first day, while **Mushfiqur Rahim** reached his 39th birthday by scoring 71 not out.  Senior assistant coach **Mohammad Salahuddin** highlighted slip catching as an area of concern after two dropped catches.
